chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fazalat, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who prays and in his garment is excrement from a human, or a cat, or a dog. Should he repeat his prayer? He said: If he did not know, then he does not repeat.

key_terms.عَذِرَةٌ: Excrement or feces, a type of najasah

ai.seo_question: Do I need to repeat my prayer if I discover impurity on my clothes after praying?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *al-asl al-suhah* (presumption of validity) in prayer when impurity is present unknowingly. It distinguishes between the state of ignorance (*jahil*) and knowledge (*'alim*), confirming that the prayer remains valid without repetition if the wearer was unaware of the *najasah* from humans, cats, or dogs. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on ease and the removal of hardship (*rukhas*) in acts of worship.
